fields.meta_title: Personal Trainer Landing Page Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a personal trainer landing page from a prompt. See four examples that turn visitors into consults, applications, and booked sessions.
fields.h1: Build a Personal Trainer Landing Page That Books Consults
fields.hero_description: Build a personal trainer landing page that turns visitors into consult requests and saves every lead to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: The Page, and Everything After the Form
fields.features_subheading: A personal trainer landing page has one job: a consult request. Emergent builds the page and what happens to each request.
fields.feature_1:
The page from one description

Describe your offer, the clients you train, and the step you want them to take. Emergent builds the page and its form from that prompt, and changes either one when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Every lead in a table you own

Each request the form takes is saved as a row in a database you own, with the name, goal, preferred days, and date. Sort the rows by goal to see what new clients ask for most.
fields.feature_3:
An alert as soon as a lead arrives

The app emails you or posts in Slack when a consult request comes in, with the client's goal in the message. A reminder follows for any request still unanswered the next morning.
fields.feature_4:
Questions that sort applicants

Ask how many hours a week someone can train, and the app routes the application by the answer. Applicants above your bar go to a review list, and the rest get your self-paced plan.
fields.feature_5:
Your tools connected over their API

The app sends each new lead to the scheduling, email, or CRM tool you already use, as long as that tool has an API. HubSpot and Stripe connect this way, and so do others.
fields.feature_6:
Your own domain, or the code

Host the page on your own domain, which uses credits, or export the page and its database code to your GitHub repository on paid plans and run it on any hosting you choose.

faq_plan.q: What is a personal trainer landing page?
How do I create a personal trainer landing page?

plan.angle: The results for this keyword are template galleries and design roundups that end at the layout; none of them follows a lead past the button. This page shows four personal trainer landing pages built from a prompt and tracks what each one does with a lead after the form is sent: a consult request that reaches the trainer with the goal attached, an online coaching application routed by weekly training hours, leads tagged by the link they came from, and a session-pack request made from a phone. Siblings stay distinct: fitness covers gyms and studios, coaching covers coaching offers broadly; this page stays on one trainer selling 1:1 training. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, what to include, page versus full website, getting clients from the page, form length, showing prices, a page about the program versus the person, taking applications, and collecting leads from people not ready to buy.
tab_stories: Marisol Vega's consult page at Vega Strength asks for a goal and preferred days, took 31 requests in October, and sends her a card with each lead's goal the moment the form lands.

Pike Online Coaching asks each applicant how many hours a week they can train; 4 hours or more sends the application to Dorian Pike's roster review, and 9 of this month's 23 applicants cleared that bar.
Koa Performance tags every lead with the link it came from, and October's report shows the bio link sent 42 of its 70 leads, the Google profile 17, and referral links 11.
Ember Lane Training lists three session packs on a phone-width page, and 9 of this month's 15 requests picked the 12-session pack at $660.
